step_by_step_reasoning: First, analyze the whiteboard to identify the main components: EKS for the multi-tenant app, Aurora for data storage, Transit Gateway for networking, Control Tower for account orchestration, and QuickSight and VPN within the provisioned tenant accounts, which connect to On-Prem Customer Data (ThirdParty). We then map the active connections: EKS connects to Aurora; QuickSight connects to Aurora via Transit Gateway; and QuickSight connects to On-Prem Customer Data via VPN.

graph.name: Summit Technology Group Loan Origination System
graph.notes: A multi-tenant loan origination system leveraging EKS and Aurora, which provisions single-tenant AWS accounts via Control Tower for secure, isolated QuickSight data visualization combined with on-premises customer data.

nodes.name: EKS
nodes.notes: Runs multi-tenant SaaS application with isolated pods per tenant.

nodes.name: Postgres Aurora
nodes.notes: Stores tenant application data using separate schemas.

nodes.name: Transit Gateway
nodes.notes: Routes traffic from tenant QuickSight accounts to the central database.

nodes.name: Control Tower
nodes.notes: Automates provisioning of isolated tenant accounts via Account Factory.

nodes.name: QuickSight
nodes.notes: Enables tenant data visualization in isolated single-tenant environments.

nodes.name: VPN
nodes.notes: Establish connection from QuickSight to customer on-premises data sources.

nodes.name: Customer On-Prem Data
nodes.notes: On-premises database containing additional community bank data.
